properties.decision: DECIDED 2026-08-08, Anthony's word: a claim may be described by a QUERY in addition to seed+depth, and an explicit stored node LIST is refused. Seed+depth remains and is unchanged for the work it already fits. WHY THE LIST IS THE ONE OPTION REJECTED, and this is the whole of the reasoning: the original choice — 'the region is COMPUTED from seed+depth rather than stored as a node list, so it follows the design as it changes' — was made to stop a claim going stale the moment the design moves. A query PRESERVES that property, because it is still evaluated fresh every time anyone reads the board; a stored list is the single option that throws it away. So this widens how a region may be DESCRIBED without weakening the guarantee the original decision bought. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: cross-cutting duties — an audit, a sweep over everything of one kind, cold-validating what another session recorded — which are a general category rather than one team's oddity, and which no radius can express. SUPERSEDES NOTHING: the seed+depth rule stands as the default; this is an addition, so the earlier choice is neither re-opened again nor un-accepted (dec:reopen-supersedes). STILL UNANSWERED and deliberately not decided here: what query language, and whether an unevaluable or empty query is refused at claim time or reported at read time. Both are build questions; the shape is settled, the surface is not.
properties.name: A claimed region may be defined by a QUERY as well as by a seed and a depth — and never by a stored node list
properties.rationale: Because the cost was measured rather than argued. dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff, 2026-08-08: their lane was 'cold-test the retrievability of nodes another session mined', spanning two unrelated slices — there is no seed whose depth-2 radius is that work. They claimed a representative node and put the truth in the `note`, so claim_report's PROSE was right while its STRUCTURED answer was wrong for them, which is the exact failure a structured board exists to remove. THE STRONGER EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL AND IT IS THREE FOR THREE: both prior workers on that lane skipped claim_region entirely and kept a text file of document paths, because a flat list described their region better than the graph could. A tool losing to a text file is the same shape as the finding that drove the read-half increment — 'today a document BEATS the graph for making a decision, and that is a fair fight the graph loses'. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT WAS PUT AND WEIGHED, not skipped: a claim is ADVISORY and never a lock, so a wrong region misleads a colleague rather than corrupting a write, which argues for keeping the mechanism simple. It was outweighed because an advisory board whose structured field is routinely wrong is how a signal gets trained into being ignored — the same objection that condemned permanently-`live` seat liveness in the same session, and the reason both were treated as real rather than cosmetic.
